# Compatibility

What this tool promises not to break, and what it deliberately does not promise.
The lists are generated from the code they describe, so a flag, a class, a check
or an exported name that appears here is one the tool actually has.

## What the numbers mean

- **Patch** — a fix. Nothing in the lists below changes; an answer may get more
  correct, and a message may get clearer.
- **Minor** — something new: a flag, a profile, a class, a check, a finding, a
  field in a document, a metric. Everything already here keeps working and keeps
  meaning what it meant.
- **Major** — something below is removed or changes meaning. That is the only
  thing a major is for.

The document schema is versioned separately and moves on its own rules — see
[the schema page](schema.md). A minor release can add a field without touching
it; only a change of *shape* moves that number.

## Deliberately not stable

None of this is an oversight, and none of it will be treated as a break:

- **The prose.** A finding's `message` and `hint`, the summary line, the text
  renderer's layout, the wording of an error. They are for people, and they get
  better. Read `check`, `status`, `class`, `value` and `unit` instead — that
  is what they are for.
- **Anything under `internal/`.** Not importable, by design: it is what lets
  those packages move.
- **`contrib/`.** Separate modules with their own dependencies and their own
  versions.
- **How many findings a run emits.** More appear as the tool learns to say more.
  The count is not a signal; the worst `status` is.
- **Timings, byte counts and measured sizes.** They describe the endpoint and the
  network, not this tool.

## Deprecation

A flag or a value that is going away keeps working for **at least two minor
releases** after it is first announced in the CHANGELOG, and says so on stderr
while it does. Removal is a major release. Nothing is ever repurposed: a name
that meant one thing does not come back meaning another.

An unknown value is always an error — never a quietly different run. That rule
has no deprecation period because it is what makes every other promise here
checkable.

## The exit status

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | the probe ran — findings are output, not an error |
| `1` | `--exit-on` matched: a finding reached that status, or an endpoint landed in that class |
| `2` | the command line was wrong, or the target list could not be read |

These three do not change without a major. A check that failed the pipeline on
every deviation is a check people route around, which is why exit 0 is the
answer whenever the probe ran at all.

## The classes

- `pq-ready` — post-quantum key exchange works, including for a client that requires it
- `pq-capable` — hybrid ML-KEM is negotiated when offered, but a post-quantum-only client did not connect
- `pq-blind` — no post-quantum support, but post-quantum-capable clients still connect on a classical group
- `pq-intolerant` — post-quantum-capable clients cannot connect at all, while classical clients can
- `pq-refusing` — post-quantum-capable clients are refused with an alert, while classical clients connect
- `no-tls13` — TLS 1.2 is the ceiling, so post-quantum key exchange is not reachable here
- `no-tls` — the plaintext upgrade to TLS was refused, so there was no handshake to grade
- `mtls-required` — the peer requires a client certificate, so no capability conclusion is available
- `unreachable` — nothing answered; no TLS conclusion available
- `tls-broken` — the port answered but no client profile completed a handshake
- `pq-other-hybrid` — post-quantum key exchange works here, but only in a hybrid group no browser sends

New classes appear in a minor release, as the tool learns to tell two
situations apart that it used to call one thing. Treat an unknown class as
unknown rather than as an error, and never as `ok`.

## The Go API — `pq/`

| Kind | Name |
|---|---|
| func | `Classes` |
| func | `Classify` |
| func | `Describe` |
| func | `Explain` |
| type | `Explanation` |
| type | `Finding` |
| type | `Options` |
| func | `Probe` |
| type | `Report` |

Struct fields are part of this surface too: a field removed or renamed is a
major, a field added is a minor. `pq/` never exposes anything from `internal/`,
which is what lets the inside move while this stays still.
